Teemore edge Devenish to win Reserve Championship title

Posted: 9:00 pm August 31, 2026
By Mark McGoldrick
m.mcgoldrick@fermanaghherald.com
SHARE
[whatsapp]

0:00 / 3:03
Instaread

TEEMORE finally got their hands on county silverware after edging out Devenish in a dramatic Reserve Grade One Championship decider at Brewster Park.

The Shamrocks had endured a remarkable run of four finals in four weeks, suffering defeat in the previous three, but they held their nerve when it mattered most to secure a hard-earned victory.

Erne Gaels Belleek focused amid bid for three-in-a-row

Advertisement

Devenish pushed them all the way, with the sides unable to be separated after normal time before Teemore found the extra-time scores required to seal the title.

Aaron Lee, Liam MacEinri and Ciaran Shannon were the heroes for Teemore as they registered the three points that ultimately decided the contest.

Close contest

It was a game that could easily have gone either way, particularly after Devenish appeared to have snatched victory late in normal time.

The Devenish side had fallen behind 0-11 to 1-07 before Teemore were penalised 50 metres for dissent.

Captain Ruairi O’Brien opted against taking the easier option and backed himself to attempt a two-point score, producing a spectacular finish which looked set to win the trophy for Devenish.

But, Oisin Donohoe had other ideas for Teemore, firing over a late leveller to force extra time.

Advertisement

The dramatic finish to normal time came after a frantic opening to the contest.

Enniskillen Gaels boosted by McShea and Jones return

Devenish struck for the game’s only goal when Jamie Flanagan’s high delivery caused panic in the Teemore defence, with O’Brien showing great determination to scramble the ball into the net.

Teemore responded through Jamie Hughes and Adam McCaffrey, but their early attacking pressure was undermined by a succession of missed opportunities.

The Shamrocks registered six wides in the opening half alone, with Devenish taking a 1-03 to 0-05 lead into the interval.

Flanagan was influential for Devenish and O’Brien added scores from placed balls, while Kyle Gallagher also produced a fine effort from play.

Teemore needed to improve after the break and their bench made a telling contribution.

Dramatic decider

The introduction of Liam MacEinri, Brandon Beattie and Lorcan McGrath, all with senior experience, added greater composure and energy to the Shamrocks’ attack.

Aaron Lee began to find his range from frees, while Nathan McGoldrick produced two excellent scores for Devenish as the lead changed hands several times.

The game remained finely balanced throughout the second half, with Lee and Donohoe eventually bringing the teams level at 1-06 to 0-09.

McGoldrick edged Devenish back in front before Lee restored Teemore’s advantage.

Veteran Ruairi Maguire then gave the Shamrocks the lead for the first time, setting up the thrilling finale.

Fermanagh Herald launches Club Championship Team of Week

Despite both sides continuing to struggle in front of the posts, neither was willing to give an inch.

Teemore’s finishing remained frustrating, with their tally of 16 wides highlighting how close the game could have been.

But when the decisive moments arrived in extra time, the Shamrocks showed greater composure.

Lee, MacEinri and Shannon all found the target, giving Teemore the cushion they needed.

Devenish battled until the final whistle but could not find a response, as Teemore rejoiced following their historic win in Enniskillen.
